steps.body: Every function family has a simplest member — its **parent function**. Algebra 2's five headliners: the line **y = x**, the parabola **y = x²**, the V of **y = |x|**, the half-curve **y = √x**, and the S-curve **y = x³**. Everything later is one of these shapes moved, flipped, or stretched.
Match each rule to the shape of its graph.

widget.prompt: Connect each parent function to its graph's shape.

pairErrors.feedback: x² is smoothly curved everywhere — the sharp corner belongs to |x|, whose two straight arms meet at a point.
|x| is built from two straight rays, so it has a corner at 0 — the smooth U is x².
x³ takes every x, negative included — the half-curve that starts at a point is √x, which needs x ≥ 0.

widget.missFeedback: Think about corners vs. smooth curves, and which rule refuses negative inputs.
widget.successFeedback: All four matched — you can now spot each family on sight.

steps.body: The two look-alikes: **x²** and **|x|** both open upward and never dip below 0 — but |x| has a **sharp corner** and straight arms, while x² is **smoothly curved**. And **√x** is the only parent that refuses negative inputs, so its graph is just half a curve.

explanationVariants: Only y = |x| is built from two straight rays meeting at the origin — that meeting point is the sharp corner.
Absolute value switches rules at 0 (−x on the left, x on the right), and the switch shows up as a corner.

widget.prompt: Which parent function's graph has a sharp corner at the origin?

options.label: y = |x|
options.feedback: Right — two straight rays meet at (0, 0), making a corner.

options.label: y = x²
options.feedback: The parabola is smoothly curved at its vertex — no corner. The corner belongs to |x|, whose straight arms meet at a point.

options.label: y = √x
options.feedback: √x starts at (0, 0) but curves smoothly away — it ends at a point rather than bending through one. The corner is |x|'s.

options.label: y = x³
options.feedback: The cubic flattens through the origin smoothly — an S-curve has no corner. |x| is the one with straight arms meeting sharply.

widget.prompt: Trace y = x³ to x = 2 and read the height.
widget.successFeedback: y = 8, since 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. A cube is three copies multiplied, not three copies added — the trace shows the curve climbing far faster than a straight line as x grows, which is the visual signature of that difference.
widget.lowFeedback: Still to the left of x = 2.

steps.body: Which parent is picky about inputs?
explanationVariants: You can't take the square root of a negative (in the real numbers), so y = √x only accepts x ≥ 0.
√x asks 'what squared gives x?' — no real number squares to a negative, so negative x is refused.

widget.prompt: Which parent function is only defined for x ≥ 0?

options.label: y = √x
options.feedback: Right — square roots of negatives aren't real, so √x accepts only x ≥ 0.

options.label: y = x²
options.feedback: You can square ANY number — (−3)² = 9 works fine. It's the square ROOT that refuses negatives.

options.label: y = x³
options.feedback: Cubing a negative is fine: (−2)³ = −8. Every real x works for the cubic.

options.label: y = |x|
options.feedback: Absolute value happily takes negatives — |−5| = 5. It's √x that refuses them.

explanationVariants: |−5| asks for the distance from −5 to 0, which is 5.

widget.prompt: For the parent y = |x|, what is y when x = −5?

commonErrors.feedback: Absolute value strips the sign — it measures distance from 0, and distance is never negative: |−5| = 5.
That's (−5)² — squaring. Absolute value doesn't multiply; it just drops the sign: |−5| = 5.

widget.fallbackFeedback: |−5| is the distance from −5 to 0 on the number line: 5.

steps.body: Identify a parent from its description.
explanationVariants: Falling on the left, rising on the right, smooth through the origin with no corner — that S shape is the cubic y = x³.
y = x keeps a constant slope (straight line); x² and |x| both open UP on both sides. Only x³ falls left and rises right through a smooth S.

widget.prompt: A graph is S-shaped: it falls on the far left, rises on the far right, passes smoothly through the origin, and has no corner. Which parent is it?

options.label: y = x³
options.feedback: Right — the cubic's ends go opposite directions, and it flattens smoothly through (0, 0).

options.label: y = x
options.feedback: The line also falls left and rises right — but it's perfectly straight, not S-shaped with a flattening bend at the origin.

options.label: y = x²
options.feedback: The parabola rises on BOTH far ends — it never falls on the left the way this graph does.

options.label: y = |x|
options.feedback: The V rises on both sides and has a sharp corner — this graph is smooth and falls on the left.

hints: Check the far ends first: this graph falls on the left and rises on the right.
x² and |x| rise on BOTH ends — rule them out. That leaves the line and the cubic.
A line is straight everywhere; an S shape that flattens through the origin is the cubic.

steps.body: Five parents, five shapes — the raw material for every transformation.
takeaways: The parents: y = x, y = x², y = |x|, y = √x, y = x³.
|x| has a sharp corner; x² is the smooth look-alike; √x only takes x ≥ 0.
Every later function is a parent moved, flipped, or stretched.
steps.teaser: Next: which inputs a function actually accepts — the domain.

concept.body: Match shapes to rules: straight line = x, smooth U = x², sharp V = |x|, half-curve from a point = √x, S-curve = x³.

explanationVariants: The V with a sharp corner at the origin is y = |x| — two straight rays meeting at a point.
x² would be a smooth U; the CORNER gives away absolute value.

widget.prompt: A graph is a V: two straight rays meeting in a sharp point at the origin. Which parent is it?

options.label: y = |x|
options.feedback: Right — straight arms and a sharp corner are absolute value's signature.

options.label: y = x²
options.feedback: The parabola curves smoothly — no straight arms, no corner. The V is |x|.

options.label: y = √x
options.feedback: √x is only HALF a curve (x ≥ 0 side) — a full V on both sides is |x|.
